article_title: Incorporating the Stern-Gerlach delayed-choice quantum eraser into the undergraduate quantum mechanics curriculum
citation: Courtney, W. F., Vieira, L. B., Julienne, P. S., & Freericks, J. K. (2017). Incorporating the Stern-Gerlach delayed-choice quantum eraser into the undergraduate quantum mechanics curriculum. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.02670
title: 171Yb atomic-clock states as a proposed physical system for the Stern-Gerlach quantum eraser, limited by small nuclear magnetic moment
description: The article proposes the 171Yb atom as a candidate for realizing the scheme: "The system is the 171Yb atom, a species known to enable an ultra-accurate optical frequency atomic clock." Its two J = 0 clock states (1S0 and 3P0) leave the electronic angular momentum unchanged on excitation, and the weak coupling to nuclear spin makes the electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom essentially independent. The challenge is that the nuclear magnetic moment is nearly 2000 times smaller than the electron magnetic moment, so "achieving practical separations with a small nuclear magnetic moment requires impractically large magnetic ﬁeld gradients." The authors suggest the optical Stern-Gerlach effect, already demonstrated for nuclear spin separation in Yb and Sr, might achieve the needed separations.
requirements: Transitions between the internal states must not change the total electronic angular momentum, and the excited-state lifetime must be long enough for the experiment
constraints: The small nuclear magnetic moment requires impractically large magnetic field gradients; whether a practical optical Stern-Gerlach design is possible would need careful consideration since the ground and excited states do not generally experience the same optical forces
examples: The optical Stern-Gerlach separation of nuclear spin components has already been demonstrated with 171Yb, 173Yb, and 87Sr using the intensity gradient of a focused laser beam.
